text.p: The commercial real estate assets being spun off by Lennar Corp should be worth $18 to $24 a share, and the combined Lennar-Pacific Greystone Corp should be worth about $15 a share, Southeast Research Partners said Wednesday.
"The sum of the two parts is worth more than the whole," said Southeast analyst Timothy Jones. "I recommended customers buy (Lennar) up to $30, but obviously I think it's worth more."
Lennar shares were up three points at 29-3/8 in morning trading, off a session high of 30-1/4, a new 52-week peak.
Jones said he had recommended Lennar as a buy since November.

The planned spinoff of the finance and commercial real estate assets into LPC Inc is giving investors a chance to mark up substantially the joint ventures, troubled mortgage securities and other properties Lennar bought in the early 1990s, he said.
Lennar and Greystone announced a merger deal before the stock market opened. Lennar said it was creating LPC and spinning it off to its shareholders.
Jones said he estimated that the pro forma earnings of LPC Inc for 1997 would be about $1.55 a share, with an earnings multiple of 12 to 16.
The combined Lennar-Greystone pro forma 1997 earnings would be about $1.38 a share, with a likely multiple of 15, he said.
After the merger and spinoff, he said, Lennar will have leading spots in the three top states for home building -- Texas, California and Florida.
